_doc: BBB-tier covenant + operating metrics — chunk A (10 obligors). Hospital MTIs typically state a DSCR rate covenant; days-cash-on-hand floors often live in bank/swap/credit agreements. Where verified, we record both the value and source. Where not verified, we mark LOW confidence with industry-typical defaults (65 days DCOH / 1.10x DSCR for BBB-tier hospital MTI).
_methodology: WebSearch + WebFetch against (1) rating-agency reports (Moody's/Fitch/S&P press releases & credit opinions), (2) Bond Buyer / Becker's trade press coverage of rating actions, (3) obligor IR / continuing disclosure pages, (4) MSRB EMMA where reachable, (5) state regulatory financial filings (MD HSCRC, MA CHIA, etc.). PDFs from EMMA and continuing disclosure often returned binary/encoded content not parseable by WebFetch; we relied on rating-agency snippet text and trade press where that occurred.

_confidence_definitions.HIGH: Direct from MTI / Official Statement / continuing disclosure with verbatim numeric covenant value
_confidence_definitions.MEDIUM: Rating-agency report or trade press summary quoting the specific covenant value for THIS obligor
_confidence_definitions.LOW: Industry-typical default applied (no verified source for this obligor's specific covenant)

_patterns_observed.covenant_tightness: BBB-tier hospital MTIs do NOT systematically have tighter covenants than AA-tier — the typical 1.10x DSCR / 65-75 DCOH floors are roughly constant across rating tiers (per UPMC, CommonSpirit, Cleveland Clinic reference set in covenant_terms.json). What differs is the CUSHION between actual metrics and the covenant floor. OU Health (45/40 DCOH covenants), UofL Health (30 DCOH actual), and Frederick Health (operating losses) are at high covenant-pressure risk. Hurley is the outlier with stricter 1.20x DSC and 80 DCOH on 2016 series.
_patterns_observed.data_quality_pattern: Trade press (Bond Buyer, Becker's, Healthcare Finance News) and rating agency press releases are the most accessible source for SOME covenant data, but verbatim numeric covenant values are rarely quoted unless the obligor is in breach or near-breach. Official Statement PDFs from EMMA/state conduits return binary content via WebFetch and require direct browser access or pyPDF extraction.
